target.title: fix(mattermost): truncate inbound preview on code-point boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mattermost inbound handler in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` builds a verbose log preview with `bodyText.slice(0, 200)`. When an emoji or other astral character straddles the 200 UTF-16 code-unit boundary, that raw slice can emit a **lone surrogate** into the preview string. Downstream consumers that expect well-formed UTF-16 can reject or mis-render the preview.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw `.slice(0, 200)` with the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the surrogate-safe preview pattern already used by Slack, Discord, Telegram, IRC, Line, MS Teams, and Feishu channel previews.

## User Impact

Cosmetic logging only: when the 200th code unit would split an emoji, the verbose inbound preview now omits the partial emoji instead of logging a broken surrogate. No message delivery or routing behavior changes.

## Evidence

The regression now runs through the real monitor path rather than duplicating
the truncation expression in a standalone helper test. It emits a websocket
`posted` event whose 200th UTF-16 unit is half of an emoji, enables verbose
logging through the runtime mock, and asserts the exact production log line:
199 complete ASCII characters, with no dangling surrogate.

Exact-head hosted CI is the execution gate for this contributor branch. A fresh
branch autoreview completed cleanly with 0.99 confidence.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — verbose log preview may omit a trailing emoji when truncation would have split its surrogate pair.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No
- Highest-risk area: verbose logging only
- Mitigation: matches sibling channel preview truncation behavior; message handling unchanged

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Maintainer-reviewed production-path regression coverage
